basis: Repository selection and configuration history, not installation or activation dates. A bar ends only when a linked event replaces, updates or removes it. Additions on separate tracks coexist. Uncommitted changes remain undated.

stages.label: Firefox
stages.detail: Firefox configuration is present in the initial repository snapshot; the installation date is not established.

stages.label: Zen
stages.detail: Zen replaces the Firefox application module and browser settings.

stages.label: LibreWolf
stages.detail: Browser module selection changes; personal usage dates remain unknown.

stages.label: Brave Origin
stages.detail: Program imports and web MIME defaults change; not a claim about exclusive usage.

stages.label: GNOME
stages.detail: Previous desktop session; its initial adoption date is not recorded.

stages.label: Niri + Noctalia
stages.detail: GNOME remained available while the new desktop was integrated.

stages.label: GNOME session removed
stages.detail: GNOME session removed; GNOME/GTK applications and integration remain.

stages.label: Store-managed Niri
stages.detail: Home Manager deployment replaces direct out-of-store links.

stages.label: NixOS 26.11 · unstable
stages.detail: The initial locked Nixpkgs revision declares release line 26.11, and the current source pin also declares 26.11. This is source/channel history, not evidence of an installed-release transition. stateVersion controls compatibility defaults and must not be read as the running OS version.

stages.label: Noctalia v5 · unpinned
stages.detail: The Noctalia input and shell integration are introduced alongside Niri. This records repository selection, not a firmware or OS release.

stages.label: Noctalia v5.0.1
stages.detail: The flake selects the v5.0.1 release; Noctalia remains the shell.

stages.label: Noctalia v5.1.0
stages.detail: The Noctalia release pin advances to v5.1.0.

stages.label: Noctalia v5.2.0
stages.detail: Repository release-pin update, not the upstream release or activation date.

stages.label: Noctalia v5.2.1
stages.detail: The separate Noctalia flake input is pinned to v5.2.1. A later configuration update changes package and module ownership.

stages.label: Noctalia · Nixpkgs
stages.detail: The separate release-pinned input is removed. Home Manager's built-in module and the Nixpkgs package now own the shell integration. This records configuration ownership, not an activation date or a guessed release version.

stages.label: COSMIC apps
stages.detail: GNOME applications replace these integrations; desktop compositor remained Niri.

stages.label: GNOME apps
stages.detail: An application-stack change, not a COSMIC compositor migration.

stages.label: micro
stages.detail: Previous editor defaults; not an installation date.

stages.label: Helix / Zed
stages.detail: EDITOR and VISUAL change; this is not their first installation date.

stages.label: Zed · Oxc / Oxfmt
stages.detail: Zed adopts workspace Oxc/Oxfmt, Tombi, scoped save actions, navigation keymaps and centrally declared subscription-agent defaults. This extends the existing editor setup; account authentication and editor behavior remain runtime checks.

stages.label: Jovian integration
stages.detail: Previous gaming integration; adoption date unknown.

stages.label: Standard Steam
stages.detail: Simpler desktop gaming ownership without a dedicated Jovian session.

stages.label: LUKS / Btrfs / Preservation
stages.detail: Tmpfs root, encrypted Btrfs and explicit persistence are a baseline, not a proven adoption date. The later scrub, SMART and zRAM additions do not replace this foundation.

stages.label: Scrub / SMART
stages.detail: Monthly scrub and SMART added. Retained logs changed again later; always consult the current persistence declaration.

stages.label: zRAM + disk swap
stages.detail: Compressed RAM swap reduces disk pressure; disk swap remains overflow.

stages.label: Default kernel set
stages.detail: Previous kernel policy; numeric version and start date unknown.

stages.label: Latest kernel set
stages.detail: Hardware-support policy changed; this does not identify a numeric kernel version.

stages.label: Power Profiles Daemon
stages.detail: Present in the first snapshot and committed HEAD. No recorded TLP, TuneD or auto-cpufreq migration.

stages.label: sudo
stages.detail: Previous sudo implementation; initial installation date is not established.

stages.label: sops-nix
stages.detail: Encrypted declarative host secrets are added; identities remain in persistent storage.

stages.label: sudo-rs
stages.detail: Rust sudo replaces the C sudo implementation. This does not replace the independent AppArmor or secret-management layers.

stages.label: AppArmor support
stages.detail: AppArmor is enabled as an additional access-control layer. Enablement is not proof of complete application confinement.

stages.label: USBGuard + kernel hardening
stages.detail: USB authorization policy and further kernel hardening are added alongside existing privilege and secret-management controls.

stages.label: DNSCrypt
stages.detail: NetworkManager stops owning DNS; resolver configuration was corrected the following day.

stages.label: Explicit DNS providers
stages.detail: Cloudflare and Scaleway replace discovery across the full catalog.

stages.label: Loopback / native VPN
stages.detail: Loopback resolver alignment, Kavita LAN opening removed, native NetworkManager VPN workflow documented.

stages.label: Flat host / user layout
stages.detail: shadow/ directly selects modules; no extra profiles layer is needed for one host/user.

stages.label: Operator cheatsheet
stages.detail: CHEATSHEET.md preceded the interactive guide.

stages.label: Interactive guide
stages.detail: Offline lessons, app catalog and simulations become the operator entry point.

stages.label: Minimal technical handbook
stages.detail: The guide changes to a compact source-based handbook. The Hugo migration and later relationship-aware timeline are separate subsequent changes.

stages.label: Hugo · source-driven pages
stages.detail: The handbook migrates to a local Hugo theme with separate section pages, a generated release watchlist, explicit history relationships, offline output and a GitHub Pages build workflow. Later navigation and search improvements extend this foundation.
